note: spring5-security-batch round 3: `exception java.io.IOException is never thrown in body of corresponding try statement` after the Base64 port (TokenCodec.decode) → catch what Base64 decoding throws — L2 `compile|other|exception java.io.ioexception is never thrown in body of corresponding try statement` (6954585468)
response:
<analysis>TokenCodec.decode wrapped sun.misc.BASE64Decoder.decodeBuffer (throws IOException for bad input) in try / catch (IOException e) → IllegalArgumentException("bad token"). java.util.Base64 throws no IOException; bad input raises IllegalArgumentException, so the catch has to name that to keep the behaviour. The script changes the catch on the reported lines, only where the try block decodes with java.util.Base64 (other IOException catches are left alone and logged).</analysis>
<script>
import re


def fix(p):
    lines_by_file = {}
    for e in p.errors:
        if e.get("file") and e.get("line") and p.exists(e["file"]):
            lines_by_file.setdefault(e["file"], set()).add(int(e["line"]))
    for path, lines in sorted(lines_by_file.items()):
        rows = p.read(path).split("\n")
        changed = 0
        for ln in sorted(lines):
            i = ln - 1
            if not (0 <= i < len(rows)) or "catch (IOException" not in rows[i]:
                p.log(f"{path}:{ln}: no catch (IOException ...) on this line")
                continue
            body = "\n".join(rows[max(0, i - 8):i])
            if "Base64.get" not in body[body.rfind("try"):]:
                p.log(f"{path}:{ln}: the try block does not decode with java.util.Base64 - left alone")
                continue
            rows[i] = rows[i].replace("catch (IOException", "catch (IllegalArgumentException", 1)
            changed += 1
        if changed:
            p.write(path, "\n".join(rows))
        p.log(f"{path}: {changed} catch clause(s) -> IllegalArgumentException")
</script>
